papers.title: Differential evolution of neuroinflammatory remodeling programs related to scar formation and regeneration in spinal cord injury: A cross-species multi-omics analysis.
papers.abstract: Spinal cord injury in mammals often transitions from an acute inflammatory response to persistent neuroinflammatory and scar-associated remodeling, whereas zebrafish attenuate injury-induced inflammatory programs during regenerative repair. The molecular programs underlying these divergent outcomes remain incompletely understood. In this study, we integrated phase-aligned mouse and zebrafish spinal cord injury datasets using single-cell and single-nucleus transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, pathway and regulon analyses, expression-based ligand-receptor co-expression analysis, machine-lea
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell, single-nucleus, and spatial transcriptomics from mouse and zebrafish spinal cord injury models to compare how neuroinflammatory and scar-associated remodeling programs diverge across species. By aligning injury phases and applying pathway, regulon, ligand-receptor, and machine-learning analyses, the authors identify molecular programs that distinguish persistent mammalian scarring from zebrafish regenerative repair. The work highlights cross-species differences in inflammatory resolution as candidate targets for promoting regeneration.

papers.title: Standardizing spatial transcriptomic analysis for infectious diseases with STID.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomic studies of infectious diseases still rely on fragmented data analysis processes. Here, we developed STID (spatial transcriptomics toolkit for infectious diseases), a standardized framework for spatial transcriptomic analysis of infectious diseases that leverages the Seurat ecosystem and incorporates Python-based modules. STID provides an extensible infection-specific data structure and supports a full suite of analyses, such as pathogen background correction, infection-associated spot and niche identification, single-sample niche characterization, and multi-sample compar
papers.summary: STID is a standardized framework for analyzing spatial transcriptomics data from infectious disease studies, built on the Seurat ecosystem with Python modules. It provides an infection-specific data structure and supports pathogen background correction, identification of infection-associated spots and niches, single-sample niche characterization, and multi-sample comparisons. This addresses the fragmented analysis pipelines currently used in the field.

papers.title: Multi-omics analysis of high-grade serous ovarian cancers reveals heterogeneity and distinct immunological patterns based upon clinico-genomic status.
papers.abstract: High-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) is characterized by remarkable intratumoral heterogeneity and variable tissue architectures, dictating differential therapeutic responses. Although BRCA1/2 mutations correlate with improved responses to DNA-damaging agents, how BRCA genotype shapes the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) remains incompletely understood. Here, we integrated whole exome sequencing, total RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to profile a cohort of BRCA-mutated (BRCA-MT) and non-BRCA-mutated (BRCA-WT) HGSOC tumors. While bulk transcriptomics highlighted global phenot
papers.summary: This study integrates whole-exome sequencing, bulk RNA sequencing, and spatial transcriptomics to profile high-grade serous ovarian cancers stratified by BRCA mutation status. It finds that BRCA-mutated and BRCA-wild-type tumors differ in tumor immune microenvironment composition and spatial organization, revealing heterogeneity in immunological patterns linked to clinico-genomic status. These findings suggest BRCA genotype shapes immune contexture, with implications for therapy response.

papers.title: Advances in Single-Cell and Spatial Omics for Glioblastoma Precision Medicine.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma is the most aggressive and fatal primary malignant brain tumour in adults, characterised by extensive intra-tumour heterogeneity, diffuse infiltration into surrounding brain tissue. Despite advances in surgery, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy, patient prognosis remains poor, underscoring the critical need for improved biological insight to guide precision medicine potential strategies. Although traditional bulk genomic and transcriptomic analyses have made a substantial contribution to understanding glioblastoma pathophysiology, such average molecular signals across cell population
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell and spatial omics technologies are being applied to glioblastoma, an aggressive brain tumor with extensive cellular heterogeneity and diffuse infiltration. It argues that these higher-resolution approaches overcome the limitations of bulk genomic and transcriptomic analyses, which average signals across cell populations and obscure the tumor's true complexity. The authors highlight how these technologies could inform precision medicine strategies for glioblastoma.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell transcriptomics with computational pathology to identify a stem-like epithelial population in bladder cancer marked by C11orf24. This population is linked to remodeling of the tumor microenvironment and to immune evasion, suggesting a role in disease progression and therapeutic resistance.

papers.title: A multi-omics study integrating single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics, and mendelian randomization unveil the implication of TRDMT1 expression in T cells on the immunotherapeutic response and prognosis in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: m5C, an important RNA modification, is closely associated with breast cancer; however, their causal relationship is unknown. We examined the relationship between m5C regulation and breast cancer. Genome-wide association study breast cancer data and expression quantitative trait loci of m5C regulatory factor genes in blood were collected. We explored the causal relationship among m5C regulatory genes, breast cancer susceptibility, and prognosis through Mendelian randomization. Single-cell RNA sequencing data from peripheral blood mononuclear cells of patients with breast cancer and healthy cont
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with Mendelian randomization to investigate how m5C RNA modification regulators, particularly TRDMT1, influence breast cancer susceptibility, prognosis, and immunotherapy response. The authors identify TRDMT1 expression in T cells as a potentially causal factor affecting immunotherapeutic outcomes, linking an RNA modification pathway to clinical breast cancer phenotypes.

papers.title: Computational deconvolution of drug sensitivity via single-cell-to-bulk transcriptome mapping.
papers.abstract: Analyses routinely conducted in both fundamental research and biomedical studies often report aggregate signals derived from heterogeneous mixtures of cells. These mixtures reflect the intrinsic anatomical and functional complexity of the tissues and organs from which they are derived. Such bulk measurements obscure cell-specific signals, thereby hindering accurate interpretation of the underlying biological processes. Here, we introduce CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and expression, and then resolves bulk drug se
papers.summary: The authors present CLIMB and CLIFF, a two-step machine-learning framework that first deconvolves bulk RNA-seq into cell-type composition and cell-type-specific expression, then uses this to resolve bulk drug sensitivity signals. This enables drug response to be attributed to specific cell populations within heterogeneous tissue samples.

papers.title: CDState Resolves Malignant Cell Heterogeneity from Bulk Tumor RNA Sequencing Data.
papers.abstract: Intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity (ITTH), defined as the coexistence of diverse cell states within a single tumor, complicates cancer treatment and contributes to variable therapeutic responses. Although single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) can resolve this complexity, its cost and technical demands limit large-scale use. Bulk RNA-seq provides a scalable alternative but requires computational methods to deconvolve bulk transcriptomes into distinct cell states. Existing supervised approaches rely on accurate reference data, which are lacking for many cancer types, whereas unsupervised
papers.summary: CDState is a computational method that deconvolves bulk tumor RNA sequencing data into distinct malignant cell states, capturing intratumor transcriptional heterogeneity without requiring single-cell reference data. By resolving cell-state composition from bulk transcriptomes, it offers a scalable alternative to scRNA-seq for studying tumor heterogeneity across large cohorts. This could enable broader analyses of how cell-state diversity affects treatment response.

papers.title: Donor-aware integration of public single-cell and spatial transcriptomes identifies a VIC remodeling program and FN1-NT5E spatial association in calcific aortic valve disease.
papers.abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) involves interacting endothelial, interstitial, immune and extracellular-matrix programs, but public single-cell studies contain many cells and few donors. A staged, donor-aware computational workflow was applied to five public human transcriptomic datasets. GSE220774 was used for single-cell discovery; GSE51472, GSE194180 and GSE235995 for fixed-signature replication; and GSE306288 for donor-level spatial assessment. Donors or patients, rather than cells or spots, were treated as biological replicates. VIC9 ranked highest for a prespecified fibrocalcific c
papers.summary: This study applies a donor-aware computational workflow to five public human transcriptomic datasets to study calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD), treating donors rather than individual cells or spots as biological replicates to avoid pseudoreplication. The authors identify a valvular interstitial cell (VIC) remodeling program (VIC9) associated with fibrocalcific progression and report a spatial association between FN1 and NT5E in donor-level spatial transcriptomics data.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19.
papers.abstract: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19. We report a progressive loss of endothelial cell types, pneumocytes type I and natural killer cells coupled with a continuous increase of myeloid and stromal cells, mostly peribronchial fibroblasts, across acute and proliferative DAD. Spatial organization analysis also identified specific compartme
papers.summary: Using Visium spatial transcriptomics on lung samples from fatal COVID-19 cases and controls, the authors map how cell composition and gene expression change across progressive stages of diffuse alveolar damage. They find a progressive loss of endothelial cells, type I pneumocytes, and natural killer cells, alongside an increase in myeloid and stromal cells (especially peribronchial fibroblasts). Spatial analysis also reveals distinct tissue compartments associated with disease progression.

papers.title: Cellular scaling laws in the mammalian brain.
papers.abstract: Recent whole-brain cell atlases have uncovered a consistent cytoarchitectural feature: the greatest diversity of discrete neuronal cell types resides not in the regions with the most neurons (e.g., the cortex and cerebellum) but rather in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem. We propose that this discrepancy reflects a fundamental algorithmic division in the vertebrate brain between a "learning subsystem" and a "steering subsystem." The learning subsystem (cortex, striatum, and cerebellum) scales via the replication of repetitive modules to maximize computational ca
papers.summary: The paper proposes that whole-brain cell atlases reveal a consistent pattern: the highest diversity of neuronal cell types is found in deep subcortical structures like the hypothalamus and brain stem, not in neuron-rich regions like the cortex and cerebellum. The authors interpret this as evidence for two distinct subsystems in the vertebrate brain—a "learning subsystem" (cortex, striatum, cerebellum) that scales by replicating repetitive modules, and a "steering subsystem" (subcortical structures) that scales through cell-type diversification.

papers.title: The gene expression signature of multinucleated giant cells in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice.
papers.abstract: Multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) are associated with chronic inflammation and infectious diseases, but their biological characteristics in vivo remain poorly understood because intact cells are difficult to isolate from tissues. In visceral leishmaniasis, heavily parasitized, hemophagocytic MGCs are observed in the spleens of Leishmania donovani-infected mice, suggesting that these cells may contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology. In this study, we established a method for isolating intact MGCs from the spleens of chronically infected BALB/c mice and performed transcriptomic
papers.summary: The authors developed a method to isolate intact multinucleated giant cells (MGCs) from the spleens of mice chronically infected with Leishmania donovani, a parasite causing visceral leishmaniasis. They then profiled the transcriptome of these cells, providing the first gene expression signature of tissue MGCs in this infection context. This work opens the door to understanding how these poorly characterized cells contribute to parasite persistence and disease pathology.

papers.title: Integrative bulk and single-cell transcriptomics identifies a HERC5-linked immune-attenuated risk program for pulmonary metastasis/relapse in osteosarcoma.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary metastasis/relapse (PM/R) is a major cause of osteosarcoma treatment failure. We aimed to develop a compact transcriptomic PM/R risk score and characterize associated immune and single-cell programs.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomic data to build a compact risk score for predicting pulmonary metastasis or relapse in osteosarcoma, identifying a HERC5-linked program associated with immune attenuation. The work links a specific gene signature to an immunosuppressed tumor microenvironment and characterizes the underlying single-cell programs.

papers.title: SPP1⁺ macrophage-derived WNT5A contributes to MMP11⁺ myCAF-mediated matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the leading subtype of non-small cell lung cancer. However, the stromal-immune circuits that coordinate matrix remodeling and immunotherapy resistance in LUAD remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to characterize the stromal-immune interactions associated with LUAD progression and poor response to PD-1 blockade.
papers.summary: This study identifies a stromal-immune circuit in lung adenocarcinoma in which SPP1⁺ macrophages secrete WNT5A to drive MMP11⁺ myofibroblastic cancer-associated fibroblasts (myCAFs) and matrix remodeling, contributing to resistance to PD-1 blockade. The work links specific macrophage and fibroblast subpopulations to immunotherapy failure, suggesting candidate targets for combination strategies.

papers.title: A cellular view of seed development and germination.
papers.abstract: Seeds are fundamental to global food security, yet their encapsulated structure, dense storage compounds, and spatial heterogeneity have created a "hidden box" problem, often restricting research to bulk and tissue approaches that mask cell type-specific regulatory programs. Advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics now enable systematic dissection of seed biology at cellular resolution. This review provides a cellular view spanning the developmental continuum from fertilization to seedling establishment by synthesizing single-cell and spatial transcriptomic studies in Arabidopsis th
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent single-cell and spatial transcriptomics studies of Arabidopsis seed biology, covering the full continuum from fertilization through germination and seedling establishment. It argues that these cellular-resolution approaches overcome the limitations of bulk and tissue-level studies, which have masked cell type-specific regulatory programs in seeds due to their encapsulated structure and spatial heterogeneity. The review frames this as a solution to the 'hidden box' problem in seed research.

papers.title: CABOPRE: Evaluating Perioperative Cabozantinib's Efficacy and Biomarkers for Cytoreductive Nephrectomy in Advanced Renal Cell Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Despite advances in metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC), long-term survival is poor and biomarkers are lacking. Optimal integration of cytoreductive nephrectomy (CN) in the current era remains controversial. CABOPRE, the first phase II trial assessing perioperative cabozantinib in mRCC patients eligible for CN, aimed to determine its effects in this setting, integrating tumor outcomes with molecular profiling.
papers.summary: CABOPRE is the first phase II trial testing perioperative cabozantinib in patients with metastatic renal cell carcinoma who are candidates for cytoreductive nephrectomy. The study aims to assess drug efficacy in this setting and to identify molecular biomarkers by integrating tumor outcomes with molecular profiling.

papers.title: NoiBic: a noise-tolerant biclustering algorithm for high-throughput gene expression data analysis.
papers.abstract: High-throughput transcriptomic technologies generate large-scale gene expression datasets for functional module discovery. However, technical and biological noise can obscure coherent expression patterns and compromise module detection. Noise-tolerant methods are therefore needed to recover meaningful biclusters.
papers.summary: The authors present NoiBic, a biclustering algorithm designed to tolerate noise in high-throughput gene expression data. It aims to recover coherent gene-sample modules that are otherwise obscured by technical and biological noise, improving functional module discovery in transcriptomic datasets.

papers.title: PRISM-GEP: Viewing single-cell expression through the lens of topic modeling.
papers.abstract: Gene-expression programs (GEPs) are the co-regulated gene modules whose coordinated activity encodes biological processes. Recovering them from single-cell RNA-seq is hard because regulation is many-to-many. A cell can run several programs at once, and a gene can take part in several. Methods that resolve programs along a trajectory break this structure by assigning each gene to a single program.
papers.summary: PRISM-GEP applies topic modeling to single-cell RNA-seq data to recover gene-expression programs (co-regulated gene modules) without forcing each gene into a single program, preserving the many-to-many structure of regulation. This addresses a key limitation of trajectory-based methods that assign genes to only one program.

papers.title: Dermatopathology 2030: Navigating the Digital, Computational and Molecular Convergence for Precision Diagnostics-Originated from a Round Table Discussion at A 66, Basel.
papers.abstract: Background: Traditional dermatopathology relies on analog, qualitative pattern recognition, which encounters critical limitations when facing diagnostic "gray zones" and ambiguous tumor proliferations. Objectives: This paper synthesizes a comprehensive framework integrating Whole Slide Imaging (WSI), Artificial Intelligence (AI), and multi-omics to evaluate how this structural convergence redesigns diagnostic risk and safety ecosystems toward 2030. Methods: We analyze the conceptual shift from individual microscope-based observation to multiple data integration. We integrate recent algorithmic
papers.summary: This perspective piece synthesizes a round-table discussion on how dermatopathology is shifting from analog microscope-based diagnosis to an integrated digital, computational, and molecular workflow. It argues that combining whole slide imaging, AI, and multi-omics can resolve diagnostic gray zones and ambiguous tumor proliferations, redesigning risk and safety frameworks for precision diagnostics by 2030.

papers.title: Cell-Cell Communication in Embryonic Kidney Development: Insights from Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Embryonic kidney morphogenesis depends on the coordinated communication among ureteric epithelium, nephron progenitors, stroma, endothelium and differentiating nephrons. Classical studies established central roles for glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor (GDNF) signaling through the RET proto-oncogene receptor tyrosine kinase (RET), WNT-family signaling, fibroblast growth factor (FGF), bone morphogenetic protein (BMP), Notch, Hedgehog, vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF) and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF) pathways, but pathway-centered models do not fully explain why simila
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are reshaping our understanding of cell-cell communication during embryonic kidney development. It highlights that classical pathway-centered models (GDNF/RET, WNT, FGF, BMP, Notch, Hedgehog, VEGF, PDGF) are insufficient to explain the complexity of kidney morphogenesis, and that spatially resolved, cell-type-specific signaling maps offer a more complete picture. The paper serves as an integrative overview of how modern omics approaches complement and extend decades of developmental biology work.

papers.title: Single-Cell and Bulk RNA-Seq Profiling Identifies Cell Adhesion-Related Gene Signatures in Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury (CIRI) involves complex secondary damage mechanisms, including oxidative stress, inflammation, and blood-brain barrier disruption, in which cell adhesion-related genes (CARGs) play a central role. Therefore, systematically elucidating the expression and regulation of CARGs is crucial for identifying new therapeutic targets to mitigate inflammatory infiltration and preserve barrier integrity. Both single-cell and bulk transcriptomic data were obtained from the Gene Expression Omnibus database. The single-cell data were processed using Seurat, and CARG activi
papers.summary: This study combined single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data from public repositories to characterize cell adhesion-related gene expression patterns in cerebral ischemia-reperfusion injury. The authors identified cell-type-specific signatures of adhesion genes that may contribute to inflammatory infiltration and blood-brain barrier disruption after stroke. These findings suggest candidate targets for mitigating secondary injury, though validation remains limited to computational analysis.

papers.title: Integrative single-cell sequencing and machine learning analyses identify chronic inflammation and cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as drivers of adverse outcomes in ovarian cancer.
papers.abstract: Ovarian cancer remains the deadliest gynecological malignancy, with neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NACT) often leaving residual fibroblast-enriched disease.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell sequencing data with machine learning to analyze ovarian cancer, focusing on residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. It identifies chronic inflammation and specific cancer-associated fibroblast subsets as key drivers of poor clinical outcomes, suggesting these as potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Pasta, a Versatile Transcriptomic Clock, Maps the Chemical and Genetic Determinants of Aging and Rejuvenation.
papers.abstract: With the growing burden of age-related diseases, understanding and modulating the aging process has become a priority. Transcriptomic aging clocks (TACs) can track biological age but remain limited by platform dependence, tissue specificity, or restricted accessibility. To address this, we developed Pasta, a robust and broadly applicable human TAC, built using a novel 'age-shift' learning framework. Pasta accurately predicted relative age across diverse tissues and data types, including bulk and single-cell RNA-Seq as well as microarray data. Its predictions aligned with senescent and stem-lik
papers.summary: The authors developed Pasta, a transcriptomic aging clock trained with a novel 'age-shift' learning framework that predicts relative biological age across diverse tissues and platforms, including bulk and single-cell RNA-seq and microarray data. Pasta's predictions aligned with senescence and stem-like states, and the clock was used to map chemical and genetic determinants of aging and rejuvenation. This provides a versatile, platform-independent tool for studying biological age.

papers.title: Spatial biology in cancer epigenetics.
papers.abstract: Cancer develops inside organized tissue environments wherein cellular behavior is heavily influenced by local interactions and spatially restricted regulatory programs. While bulk and single-cell sequencing technologies have fundamentally revolutionized our understanding of tumor biology, these techniques often disrupt tissue architecture and therefore fail to capture the spatial context in which molecular processes occur. Spatial transcriptomics has provided important insights into tumor heterogeneity, microenvironmental organization, and cell-to-cell communication. However, gene expression a
papers.summary: This review argues that spatial transcriptomics, while valuable, captures only gene expression and misses the epigenetic regulatory programs that shape tumor behavior within intact tissue architecture. It makes the case for integrating spatial epigenomic profiling into cancer research to understand how spatially restricted regulatory programs and local cellular interactions drive tumor heterogeneity and microenvironmental organization.

papers.title: A unified developmental timeline of pigmented ocular tissues in the mouse eye.
papers.abstract: Pigmented tissues of the vertebrate eye are essential for optical performance, metabolic support, and tissue homeostasis, yet their coordinated development has been difficult to study because melanin interferes with histological and immunohistochemical analyses. Here, we apply a gentle hydrogen peroxide based bleaching method compatible with IHC for Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, and Cd34, and examined Dct/Tyrp2 expression, to generate a unified developmental atlas of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye. We also re-analyzed published single-cell RNA-seq datasets from developin
papers.summary: The authors developed a gentle hydrogen peroxide bleaching method that removes melanin pigment while preserving tissue for immunohistochemistry, allowing them to map the development of all pigmented tissues in the mouse eye on a unified timeline. They combined this with marker staining (Rpe65, Rhodopsin, ZO-1, Cralbp/Rlbp1, S100b, Cd34, Dct/Tyrp2) and reanalysis of published single-cell RNA-seq data to build a developmental atlas of pigmented ocular tissues.

papers.title: Condition-Associated Pattern Extraction and Recovery From Multi-Condition Single-Cell RNA-seq Data With CAPER.
papers.abstract: A central challenge in multi-condition single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data analysis is the disentanglement of true biological signals from unwanted variations in complex experimental designs. Current statistical and machine learning-based methods struggle with this task, often providing only visualizable embeddings, over-correcting and discarding biological signal, or failing to resolve cell-type-specific responses. Here, we present CAPER, a matrix factorization framework that explicitly disentangles shared biological states from condition-specific variations. CAPER directly outputs an
papers.summary: CAPER is a new matrix factorization framework for multi-condition scRNA-seq data that separates shared biological states from condition-specific variation, rather than just producing visual embeddings. It directly outputs condition-associated expression patterns, addressing common problems of over-correction and loss of cell-type-specific responses in existing methods.

papers.title: Normalization choice drives biological interpretation in single-cell RNA-seq cancer studies: A systematic benchmarking of 465 computational pipelines.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) has transformed our understanding of tumor heterogeneity, yet the impact of computational pipeline choices on biological conclusions remains poorly characterized. Here, we systematically benchmark 465 combinations of 5 normalization methods and 4 clustering algorithms across 3 cancer datasets encompassing over 434,000 cells. We introduce the Biological Discordance Score (BDS), a metric that quantifies how marker gene interpretation changes across pipelines. We find that normalization method choice has a greater impact on biological interpretation than clu
papers.summary: This study benchmarks 465 computational pipelines (combinations of normalization methods and clustering algorithms) across three cancer scRNA-seq datasets totaling over 434,000 cells. The authors introduce a Biological Discordance Score to quantify how marker gene interpretation shifts across pipelines, and find that normalization choice affects biological interpretation more than clustering algorithm choice. The work highlights that seemingly technical preprocessing decisions can materially change downstream biological conclusions in cancer single-cell studies.

papers.title: Molecular traces of microbial cross-kingdom migration: from the gut ecosystem to the intervertebral disc microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Low back pain is a leading cause of disability worldwide, and lumbar intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) is strongly associated with its development. Recent studies have shown that the gut microbiota (GM) and its metabolites may be involved in the occurrence and development of IVDD through the gut-disc axis. However, the key microbes mediating this process and their specific molecular mechanisms remain unclear.
papers.journal: The spine journal : official journal of the North American Spine Society
papers.summary: This study investigates the 'gut-disc axis' hypothesis, proposing that gut microbes and their metabolites migrate to intervertebral discs and contribute to disc degeneration, a major cause of low back pain. The authors aim to identify the key microbial species involved and the molecular mechanisms by which they influence the disc microenvironment, though the abstract does not yet report specific findings.

papers.title: Spatial Transcriptomic and Proteomic Analysis Identifies Novel Immune-Associated Biomarkers of Anti-PD1 Response in Metastatic Melanoma.
papers.abstract: Resistance to anti-PD1 therapy remains a major challenge in metastatic melanoma, despite long-term benefit in some patients. Since a functional dendritic cell (DC)-CD8+ T cell axis is essential for anti-PD1 response, biomarkers associated with this axis may help characterize underexplored immune states linked to resistance. Here, we further characterized poor survival predictor (PSP) biomarkers previously negatively correlated with DC-CD8+ T cell axis in melanoma, evaluating their associations with anti-PD1 response, immune infiltration, and transcriptional and proteomic signatures. Pre-treatm
papers.summary: This study uses spatial transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of pre-treatment metastatic melanoma samples to identify immune-associated biomarkers linked to anti-PD1 response. The authors characterize previously identified 'poor survival predictor' (PSP) biomarkers, showing they correlate negatively with the dendritic cell–CD8+ T cell axis and associate with resistance to anti-PD1 therapy. These findings suggest PSP biomarkers could help identify underexplored immune states underlying immunotherapy resistance.

papers.title: Integrated Spatial and Bulk Transcriptomic Analysis Identifies a Multicellular Ecosystem Involved in Progression of Young Breast Cancer.
papers.abstract: Young breast cancer (YBC), defined as diagnosis at or before the age of 40 years, is characterized by an aggressive phenotype and poor prognosis. The tumor microenvironment (TME), comprising immune and stromal cells, plays a critical role in tumor initiation and progression and is closely associated with clinical outcomes. However, alterations in cell states and the organization of multicellular ecosystems within the YBC microenvironment remain poorly understood. We analyzed 7379 bulk transcriptome samples and spatial transcriptomic data from eight samples using EcoTyper and complementary spat
papers.summary: This study combined bulk transcriptomic data from 7,379 samples with spatial transcriptomics from eight samples to characterize the tumor microenvironment in young breast cancer (diagnosed at or before age 40). Using EcoTyper and complementary spatial analyses, the authors identified a multicellular ecosystem of immune and stromal cell states associated with disease progression in this aggressive subtype. The work highlights how cell-state organization within the microenvironment differs in young breast cancer and may relate to clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Patient classification using single-cell RNA-sequencing data with deep learning convolutional neural networks.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) enables gene expression profiling at the resolution of individual cells, revealing cellular heterogeneity that is obscured in bulk RNA-seq. While this offers a powerful lens to study disease-specific changes, leveraging scRNA-seq data for patient phenotype classification remains challenging due to limited sample numbers, cell count variability, high dimensionality, and dependence on cell-type annotations. Existing tools attempt to address these issues using probabilistic models or attention mechanisms, but face limitations in scalability, interpretability
papers.summary: This paper presents a deep learning convolutional neural network approach for classifying patient phenotypes directly from single-cell RNA-sequencing data, addressing challenges like limited sample sizes, variable cell counts, and high dimensionality. The method aims to bypass dependence on cell-type annotations, offering a potentially more scalable and interpretable alternative to existing probabilistic or attention-based tools.

papers.title: FDX1 is associated with CALR abundance and JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling in myeloproliferative neoplasms.
papers.abstract: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs) are driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling, yet the metabolic programs associated with driver genotype and inflammatory remodeling remain incompletely defined.
papers.summary: This study examines the metabolic protein FDX1 in myeloproliferative neoplasms (MPNs), a group of blood cancers driven by constitutive cytokine-receptor signaling. The authors report that FDX1 expression is associated with CALR abundance and with JAK-STAT-related inflammatory signaling, suggesting a link between metabolic programs and inflammatory remodeling in MPNs. The work helps connect driver genotype to metabolic and inflammatory features of these diseases.

papers.title: Integrative computational analysis of public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets suggests a candidate association between the COX-2 pathway and CE(20:4) in colorectal adenoma-carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: The fecal lipidomic changes underlying the colorectal adenoma-carcinoma sequence remain incompletely characterized, particularly regarding the continuous metabolic trajectory and heterogeneity of precancerous adenomas. We aimed to use publicly available multi-omics data and an integrative computational framework to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in adenomas.
papers.summary: This study integrates public fecal lipidomics and transcriptomics datasets to identify candidate lipidomic features associated with a CRC-like metabolic state in colorectal adenomas. The authors report a possible association between the COX-2 pathway and the lipid species CE(20:4) along the adenoma-carcinoma progression sequence. The work is purely computational and hypothesis-generating, requiring experimental validation.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis of peripheral blood identifies NETosis-associated programs and a stratified adaptive immune suppression pattern in severe acute pancreatitis.
papers.abstract: Severe acute pancreatitis (SAP) is associated with persistent organ failure and substantial mortality, yet the transcriptomic mechanisms underlying progression from mild acute pancreatitis to severe-spectrum disease remain incompletely defined. Early identification of patients at risk of persistent organ failure remains an important unmet clinical need.
papers.summary: This study integrates peripheral blood transcriptomic datasets to identify NETosis-associated gene programs and a stratified pattern of adaptive immune suppression in severe acute pancreatitis. The findings suggest that neutrophil extracellular trap formation and immune suppression signatures may help distinguish patients progressing to severe disease and persistent organ failure.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics combined with machine learning to unravel the heterogeneity of cholangiocarcinoma and the WFDC3-mediated prognostic regulatory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma (ICC) exhibits substantial cellular heterogeneity and a complex tumor microenvironment (TME), contributing to poor clinical outcomes. Effective prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of the cellular ecosystems associated with high-risk disease remain urgently needed.
papers.summary: This study integrates single-cell and spatial multi-omics with machine learning to characterize cellular heterogeneity and the tumor microenvironment in intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma. The authors identify WFDC3 as a key mediator of prognostic regulatory mechanisms, linking specific cell populations to patient outcomes. The work aims to provide prognostic biomarkers and a deeper understanding of high-risk disease ecosystems.

papers.title: Study on tumor ecology and precision medicine strategy of oral squamous cell carcinoma based on multi-omics cell atlas.
papers.abstract: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is characterized by inter- and intratumoral heterogeneity, which complicates patient stratification and treatment. Although single-cell studies have improved the resolution of the OSCC microenvironment, the relationships among cellular states, spatial organization, immune-repertoire dynamics, and patient-level ecosystem patterns remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study constructs a multi-omics single-cell atlas of oral squamous cell carcinoma to characterize the tumor microenvironment, including cellular states, spatial organization, and immune repertoire dynamics. The authors use this atlas to define patient-level ecosystem patterns and propose a precision medicine stratification strategy for OSCC.

papers.title: Histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomic analysis identifies an ECM-associated stromal pattern in lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma with complementary proteomic and functional analyses.
papers.abstract: Lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC) is a rare but locally aggressive malignancy characterized by perineural invasion, recurrence, and limited systemic treatment options. Although extracellular matrix (ECM) remodeling is increasingly recognized as an important regulator of tumor progression, its spatial organization and functional relevance in LGACC remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This study uses histopathology-guided spatial transcriptomics on lacrimal gland adenoid cystic carcinoma (LGACC), a rare and aggressive eye tumor, to map gene expression within tissue architecture. The authors identify a distinct extracellular matrix (ECM)-associated stromal pattern, which they validate with complementary proteomic and functional experiments. The work suggests that ECM remodeling by stromal cells may play an important role in LGACC progression and could be a potential therapeutic target.

papers.title: HEXB as a Candidate Target Gene in Keloid Radiotherapy: Based on Multi-Omics Analysis and Mendelian Randomization.
papers.abstract: Keloid is a common and treatment-refractory conditions in plastic surgery and dermatology. Although radiotherapy for keloid has attracted increasing attention in recent years, its mechanism at the genetic level remains poorly characterized. This study investigated the relationship between radiation-related genes (RRGs) and keloid through an integrated multi-omics and machine learning framework, and to explore potential therapeutic agents targeting the identified key gene.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data with Mendelian randomization and machine learning to identify HEXB as a candidate gene linking radiation-related pathways to keloid formation. The authors propose HEXB as a potential therapeutic target for keloid radiotherapy, though the findings are preliminary and based on computational analysis.

papers.title: Mapping the hepatic neural niche: from three-dimensional innervation architecture to periportal interoception and human translation.
papers.abstract: The liver has traditionally been viewed as an organ regulated by circulating hormones and long-range autonomic reflexes, with its intrahepatic neural architecture receiving comparatively little systematic attention. However, recent advances in tissue clearing, three-dimensional (3D) volumetric imaging, neural tracing, and spatial omics are reshaping this view. Here we synthesize emerging evidence that the hepatic nervous system is organized around spatially defined neurovascular-cellular niches, and propose the periportal region as a dominant anatomical site for interoceptive integration, whil
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent evidence that the liver contains a spatially organized neural architecture, with the periportal region acting as a key hub for interoceptive signaling. Advances in tissue clearing, 3D imaging, neural tracing, and spatial omics are revealing neurovascular-cellular niches that reshape the traditional view of the liver as regulated mainly by circulating hormones and autonomic reflexes.

papers.title: Single-cell RNA sequencing combined with artificial intelligence to uncover immunotherapy biomarkers and decipher drug resistance mechanisms in glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma represents the most aggressive primary malignant tumor of the central nervous system, characterized by extensive intratumoral heterogeneity, profound immunosuppression, therapeutic resistance, and poor clinical outcomes. Although immunotherapy has revolutionized cancer treatment, its clinical efficacy in GBM remains limited, largely due to the complexity of the tumor ecosystem and the lack of validated predictive biomarkers. Recent advances in single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, and artificial intelligence (AI)-based computational approaches have provi
papers.summary: This review discusses how single-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, and AI-based computational methods can be combined to identify immunotherapy biomarkers and understand drug resistance in glioblastoma. It highlights that GBM's intratumoral heterogeneity and immunosuppressive microenvironment limit immunotherapy efficacy, and argues that these high-resolution technologies can reveal the cellular ecosystems and resistance mechanisms needed to develop better predictive biomarkers and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: From density to spatial function: spatial multi-omics, composite biomarker design, and therapeutic engineering of tertiary lymphoid structures in solid tumors.
papers.abstract: Tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) have emerged as clinically relevant immune niches associated with improved survival and enhanced response to immune checkpoint inhibitors across multiple solid tumors. However, translational evaluation remains dominated by density-based scoring, which inadequately captures the functional heterogeneity of histologically similar lymphoid aggregates. This review synthesizes recent advances in spatial biology that support a shift from counting TLSs to interpreting them as spatially organized immune microenvironmental units embedded within local tumor ecosystems.
papers.summary: This review argues that simply counting tertiary lymphoid structures (TLSs) in tumors is insufficient because histologically similar aggregates can differ functionally. It synthesizes spatial multi-omics approaches that reveal how TLS organization within the tumor microenvironment relates to immune function, and discusses using composite spatial biomarkers and engineering TLSs therapeutically. The key message is a shift from density-based scoring to spatially resolved functional interpretation of TLSs.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis reveals a membrane tension signature associated with tumor-stroma crosstalk in hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Dysregulated membrane tension (MT) drives tumor cell migration, invasion, and immune evasion, yet the prognostic value of MT-related genes (MTRGs) in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remains unclear.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data to build a membrane tension-related gene signature for hepatocellular carcinoma and links it to tumor-stroma crosstalk and prognosis. The work suggests that membrane tension dysregulation may serve as a prognostic and immunological marker in HCC, though the abstract provides limited detail on validation.

papers.title: An entosis-informed prognostic index for survival stratification and molecular characterization in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Entosis is an actomyosin-dependent cell-in-cell process that may culminate in lysosome-mediated entotic cell death and is implicated in tumor evolution. Its clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This study constructs a prognostic index for lung adenocarcinoma based on genes related to entosis, a cell-in-cell process implicated in tumor evolution. The index stratifies patients by survival and is linked to molecular characterization of tumors, suggesting entosis-related biology has clinical relevance in LUAD.

papers.title: GART expression is associated with a proliferative and purine-metabolic ISC-like epithelial state in ulcerative colitis.
papers.abstract: To characterize the epithelial state associated with GART expression in ulcerative colitis (UC) and determine whether this association reflects a GART-specific program or a broader proliferative and purine-metabolic phenotype.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the epithelial cell state linked to GART expression in ulcerative colitis, finding that GART marks a proliferative, purine-metabolic state resembling intestinal stem cells (ISCs). The authors examine whether this association is specific to GART or reflects a broader phenotype, providing insight into epithelial heterogeneity in UC.

papers.title: Continuous spatially informed microenvironment programs show cross-cohort concordance and context-dependent spatial organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma.
papers.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics resolves tissue organization in diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL), whereas most clinically annotated cohorts remain bulk transcriptomic datasets.
papers.summary: This study introduces a method to infer continuous, spatially informed microenvironment programs from bulk transcriptomic data by leveraging spatial transcriptomics as a reference, enabling spatial characterization of DLBCL cohorts that lack spatial data. The inferred programs show cross-cohort concordance and context-dependent spatial organization, suggesting that bulk data can be used to approximate tissue-level microenvironmental structure.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis identifies CCDC69 as a marker associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration in TNBC: development and validation.
papers.abstract: Although coiled-coil domain containing 69 (CCDC69) has been implicated in tumor biology, its role in triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) and immune regulation remains unclear. Bulk transcriptomic data, single-cell RNA sequencing datasets, and spatial transcriptomics were used to investigate the role of CCDC69 in TNBC. Germinal center B-cell (GCB) signatures were quantified using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis (ssGSEA), and their associations with CCDC69 expression were assessed using correlation, ROC, and logistic regression analyses. An independent external TNBC cohort (GSE58812)
papers.journal: Brazilian journal of medical and biological research = Revista brasileira de pesquisas medicas e biologicas
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk transcriptomics, single-cell RNA-seq, and spatial transcriptomics to show that CCDC69 expression in triple-negative breast cancer is associated with germinal center B-cell infiltration. The authors validate CCDC69 as a potential marker linked to immune regulation in an independent TNBC cohort, suggesting it may reflect the immune microenvironment of these tumors.

papers.title: Loss of CLIC3 in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes is associated with immune dysfunction and poor prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is the most common histological subtype of lung cancer, with a dismal prognosis partly attributed to immune evasion mediated by T cell dysfunction within the tumor microenvironment. However, the molecular determinants governing CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocyte functional competence remain incompletely understood. Chloride intracellular channel 3 (CLIC3) has been implicated in cancer progression, but its role in T cell immunity within the LUAD TME is unknown.
papers.summary: This study investigates the role of CLIC3, a chloride channel protein, in CD8+ cytotoxic T lymphocytes within the lung adenocarcinoma tumor microenvironment. The authors report that loss of CLIC3 in these T cells is associated with immune dysfunction and poor patient prognosis, suggesting CLIC3 as a potential determinant of T cell functional competence in LUAD.

papers.title: Integration of bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis identifies candidate hub genes and inferred regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a common chronic inflammatory disorder of the skin. Despite the availability of targeted biologics like dupilumab, heterogeneous treatment responses persist, highlighting the need for reliable biomarkers and a deeper understanding of cell-type-associated molecular programs within the tissue microenvironment.
papers.summary: This study integrates bulk and single-cell transcriptomics with spatial analysis to identify candidate hub genes and infer regulatory programs in atopic dermatitis skin. The authors aim to uncover cell-type-associated molecular programs and biomarkers that could explain heterogeneous responses to biologics like dupilumab. The work provides a multi-modal transcriptomic characterization of AD tissue microenvironment.
